target.title: fix(config): render validation array indices with brackets
target.body: ## What Problem This Solves  Config validation diagnostics currently render numeric Zod path segments with dot notation in terminal output, so array indexes look like object properties. For example, an invalid value under an agent list can surface to a human reader as `agents.list.3.tools.profile`, which is harder to read than `agents.list[3].tools.profile`.  This is a narrow, partial improvement related to #104854. It only addresses human-facing array-index path formatting for config validation diagnostics; it does not add line numbers or offending-value (`got`) rendering.  ## Why This Change Was Made  `ConfigValidationIssue.path` is a documented machine-readable dot path and is serialized through `openclaw config validate --json`. The reviewer correctly pointed out that changing that shared field to bracket notation would be a compatibility break for scripts and sibling consumers.  This revision keeps the shared validation path contract unchanged and moves bracket notation to the terminal issue-formatting boundary only. JSON output and normalized/shared validation issues continue to use dot paths such as `agents.list.0.tools.exec.commandHighlighting`.  ## User Impact  Users reading non-JSON config validation errors can now distinguish arrays from object properties:  ```text Before: agents.list.3.tools.profile: Invalid input After:  agents.list[3].tools.profile: Invalid input ```  Machine-readable consumers keep the existing representation:  ```json {   "path": "agents.list.3.tools.profile",   "message": "Invalid input" } ```  ## Evidence  Focused regression coverage now asserts both display and contract behavior:  ```ts formatConfigIssueLine(   { path: "agents.list.0.tools.exec.commandHighlighting", message: "Expected boolean" },   "-",   { pathStyle: "display" }, ) -> "- agents.list[0].tools.exec.commandHighlighting: Expected boolean"  formatConfigIssueLine(   { path: "agents.list.0.tools.exec.commandHighlighting", message: "Expected boolean" },   "-", ) -> "- agents.list.0.tools.exec.commandHighlighting: Expected boolean" ```  The CLI regression test also checks both surfaces:  ```text openclaw config validate        -> agents.list[0].tools.exec.commandHighlighting openclaw config validate --json -> agents.list.0.tools.exec.commandHighlighting ```  Validation run locally on the review-fix revision:  ```powershell corepack pnpm@11.2.2 -C D:\ZXY\Github\openclaw-pr104935-reviewfix-worktree exec vitest run src/config/validation.test.ts src/config/issue-format.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.runtime-config.config.ts --no-file-parallelism --pool threads --reporter verbose corepack pnpm@11.2.2 -C D:\ZXY\Github\openclaw-pr104935-reviewfix-worktree exec vitest run src/config/validation.test.ts src/config/issue-format.test.ts src/cli/config-cli.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.cli.config.ts --no-file-parallelism --pool threads --testNamePattern "path|config validate|numeric path|JSON" --reporter verbose git diff --check ```  Results:  - formatter + validation focused run: `2 passed`, `41 tests passed` - CLI focused run covering `config validate` and `--json`: `1 passed`, `49 tests passed`, `81 skipped` - `git diff --check`: passed  A previously attempted focused `config-misc` single-test run timed out inside the existing async snapshot test body after 120s. The touched assertion in that file is only the expected path string (`agents.list[0].sandbox` -> `agents.list.0.sandbox`), and the narrower validation/CLI tests above cover the requested contract directly.  ## Possible call chain / impact  ```text config validation failure   -> Zod issue path array   -> mapZodIssueToConfigIssue()   -> ConfigValidationIssue.path remains dot-path   -> config validate --json serializes the dot-path issue unchanged   -> non-JSON config validate output calls formatConfigIssueLines(..., { pathStyle: "display" })   -> terminal diagnostics render numeric dot segments as bracket indices ```  Affected surface is limited to human-facing `config validate` issue rendering for numeric path segments. This PR intentionally leaves shared validation issue objects, JSON output, config parsing, config get/set path syntax, plugin schema diagnostics, source line-number lookup, and bad-value rendering unchanged.  Related: #104854
